note.explanation: Atomic radius, ionization energy, electron affinity and electronegativity show regular trends in the periodic table. For example, atomic radius generally decreases across a period, while ionization energy generally increases.
examples: A carbon–carbon nucleus distance of 154 pm gives a carbon radius of 77 pm.
In Group 1, the atomic radius increases from Li to Cs.
note.checkAnswer: Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right across a period.
note.simple: Across a period, atoms generally get smaller and hold their outer electrons more strongly. Down a group, atoms generally get larger.
note.checkQuestion: How does atomic radius generally change from left to right across a period?
note.title: Periodic trends in atomic properties
steps: For atomic radius, remember: generally decreases across a period and increases down a group.
For ionization energy, remember: generally increases across a period and decreases down a group.
Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group.
For the radius of an atom bonded to an identical atom, divide the distance between the two nuclei by 2.
note.answer: Atomic radius generally decreases across a period and increases down a group; ionization energy and electronegativity generally change in the opposite direction.

written.text: The first ionization energy value of magnesium is less than the second one. Give reason.
written.finalAnswer: After the first electron is removed, the remaining electron in Mg⁺ is attracted more strongly, so more energy is needed to remove it.

written.text: How would you find the atomic radius of an atom?
written.finalAnswer: Atomic radius is half the distance between the nuclei of two identical bonded atoms.

rubric.why: The method uses the distance between the nuclei of identical bonded atoms.
rubric.how: State that the distance between the nuclei of two identical bonded atoms is measured.

rubric.why: Taking half of that distance gives the radius of one atom.
rubric.description: Explain how the measurement gives the radius.
rubric.how: State that the measured distance is divided by 2.

modelAnswer: Measure the distance between the nuclei of two identical bonded atoms.
Atomic radius = half of this distance.

written.text:
Explain the variation in the following properties in the periods giving reasons.  
(a) Atomic radius  
(b) Ionization energy
written.finalAnswer: Across a period, atomic radius generally decreases because nuclear charge increases and pulls the electrons closer. Ionization energy generally increases because the smaller radius causes stronger attraction between the nucleus and the outer electrons.

rubric.why: The direction of the atomic-radius trend is essential.
rubric.description: State the atomic-radius trend across a period.
rubric.how: State that atomic radius generally decreases from left to right.

rubric.why: Increasing nuclear charge accounts for the change in atomic radius.
rubric.description: Give the reason for the atomic-radius trend.
rubric.how: Explain that increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer to the nucleus.

rubric.why: The direction of the ionization-energy trend is essential.
rubric.description: State the ionization-energy trend across a period.
rubric.how: State that ionization energy generally increases from left to right.

rubric.why: The stronger attraction explains why removing an electron needs more energy.
rubric.description: Explain the change in ionization energy.
rubric.how: Relate the smaller radius to stronger attraction between the nucleus and outer electrons.

rubric.why: The final statement must correctly summarise both trends.
rubric.how: Conclude that radius decreases while ionization energy increases across a period.

modelAnswer: (a) Atomic radius generally decreases from left to right in a period.
The charge on the nucleus increases across the period and pulls the electrons closer to the nucleus.
(b) Ionization energy generally increases from left to right in a period.
The smaller radius gives stronger attraction between the nucleus and the outer electrons.
Therefore, more energy is needed to remove an outer electron.

examTips: A short-answer question may ask for a trend, definition, comparison or reason. State the direction clearly and give the reason.
For a descriptive question on variation across a period, earn marks by stating the trend for each property and then explaining the role of nuclear charge, atomic size and attraction.
For an atomic-radius calculation, show the measured distance and divide it by 2; include pm as the unit.
Use the word generally for trends across a period, since the values in the textbook table do not rise or fall at every single step.

explain.title: Periodicity
explain.body: Periodicity in the properties of the elements occur due to recurrence of similar electronic configuration in the outermost shells. These properties include atomic radius, ionization energy, electron affinity and electronegativity.

explain.title: Atomic radius
explain.body: Atomic radius is defined as half the distance between the nuclei of the two identical bonded atoms. It is expressed in pm(1pm = 10⁻¹²m). Across a period, atomic radius generally decreases because increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer. Down a group, it increases because a new shell is added and inner electrons shield outer electrons.

explain.title: Ionization energy
explain.body: Ionization energy is the amount of energy required to remove the most loosely bound electron from the valence shell of an isolated gaseous atom. A smaller atomic radius means stronger attraction between the nucleus and outer electrons, so ionization energy generally increases across a period and decreases down a group.

explain.title: Electron affinity
explain.body: Electron affinity is the amount of energy change when an electron is added up in the outermost shell of an isolated gaseous atom. In a group, electron affinity values decrease from top to bottom because atomic size increases and the nucleus attracts an incoming electron less strongly.

explain.title: Electronegativity
explain.body: Electronegativity of an atom is its electron-attracting ability. It is defined as the force with which an atom attracts the shared pair of electrons towards itself in a bond. It increases from left to right in a period and decreases from top to bottom in a group.

mistakes: Do not confuse atomic radius with the full distance between two identical bonded nuclei; the radius is half that distance.
Do not reverse the general trends: atomic radius increases down a group, while ionization energy and electronegativity decrease down a group.
Do not say that ionization energy is energy released when an electron is added; it is energy required to remove an electron.
When giving a trend across a period, include the reason: increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer.
